reviewMethod: Inspected all 48 formal frames through four 12-frame contact sheets, then inspected three formal full-resolution stills and full-resolution formal frames 22, 24, 26, 28, 30 and 32 around the derived detachment event.

questions.observation: The cause shot clearly establishes a moving basketball, three differently filled capped bottles, court scale and travel direction.
The fixed contact view shows continuous approach and collision with no visible position jump or pre-contact bottle response.
The blue target bottle retains its small metal cap through frame 22 before the derived detachment.
At frame 24 the cap is visibly separate from the open blue bottle neck.
Frames 24 through 32 show a continuous downward and outward cap trajectory with no teleport or authored-looking pose.
The detached body remains readable as a small cylindrical metal cap and is not confused with the ball or bottle bodies.
All three bottles respond, two fall in different directions and one remains upright, producing a plausible asymmetric outcome.
The cap event is restrained rather than explosive and adds a secondary causal beat without particles, shake or decorative debris.
The effect shot keeps the open bottle neck, detached cap and complete three-bottle response group legible at rest.
Warm court lighting, cool fill, reflections and camera continuity support the action without concealing weak contact or replacing physics.

comparisonToDevelopment: The formal physical result hash is exact. Fresh formal image bytes differ after the clean native build, but direct inspection preserves the accepted causal reading and claim ceiling.
claimCeiling: This is a Bullet breakable fixed-constraint cap event, not fracture mechanics, glass breakage, deformation or liquid simulation.
